brief: 8 mistakes I made as a first-time founder that cost me $250K.

slots.title: 1. Validation, the skipped step
slots.body: I spent six months building features no one wanted. Three users signed up. Zero paid. Talk to customers before you write code.

slots.title: 2. Hiring, the rushed fix
slots.body: I hired three senior engineers before product-market fit. Salaries burned $18K monthly. Hire slow, fire fast, stay lean.

slots.title: 3. Burn rate, the ignored math
slots.body: We spent $40K on branding and swag while churn hit 12%. Fix retention before you fix the logo. Cash is oxygen.

slots.title: 4. Perfection, the real enemy
slots.body: I rebuilt the dashboard four times before launch. Competitors shipped weekly and stole our leads. Ship scrappy, iterate daily.

slots.title: 5. Focus, the lost art
slots.body: We chased enterprise and SMB at the same time. Messaging diluted, sales cycles doubled. Pick one beachhead, dominate it, then expand.

slots.title: 6. Ego, the silent killer
slots.body: I refused to delegate product decisions. I worked 80-hour weeks and missed every signal. Founders scale by trusting their team.
